specification.problem: Bounded-occurrence Max E3LIN2: m equations, each x_a+x_b+x_c = b_k mod 2 on three distinct boolean variables, each variable in at most D equations. Goal: a string satisfying more than 1/2 of the equations, using level-one (p=1) QAOA.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny explicit instance (n about 4-6 variables, a handful of equations, no black box) with the p=1 QAOA circuit, exact statevector expectation, a grid search over (gamma,beta), and sampling with best-string selection. The D^{-1/2} and D^{-1/2}/ln D advantage proofs, the worst-case ln D analysis, and the comparison to the classical algorithm are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: number of boolean variables = number of qubits
symbols.domain: positive integer under the qubit cap

symbols.meaning: maximum number of equations containing any one variable
sign of equation k: +1 if right-hand side is 0, -1 if it is 1
the three distinct variable indices of equation k
cost operator, the number of satisfied equations
measured bit string, bit i (bits[::-1][i] in Qiskit counts) is variable i

equations.label: Cost operator
equations.description: Counts satisfied equations: the term is 1 when the parity of the three bits equals the right-hand side, otherwise 0. The sign convention is Z=+1 for bit 0.
equations.abstract_quote: each equation says that the sum of the variables mod 2 is 0 or is 1
equations.justification: Standard encoding of a parity constraint as a Z-string; the exact form is taken from the sketch and not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: p=1 QAOA state
equations.description: Level-one QAOA state. The phase separator is a product of commuting ZZZ rotations, up to a global phase, and the mixer is RX(2*beta) on every qubit.
equations.abstract_quote: We apply our recent Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm [1]
equations.justification: The abstract names level-one QAOA. The exact angle conventions are standard background and are not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Angle sign and scale convention may be flipped, because the grid search covers both signs

equations.label: Per-equation gate decomposition
equations.latex: e^{i\gamma s_k Z_aZ_bZ_c/2}=\mathrm{CX}_{a\to c}\,\mathrm{CX}_{b\to c}\,R_Z^{(c)}(-\gamma s_k)\,\mathrm{CX}_{b\to c}\,\mathrm{CX}_{a\to c}
equations.description: The CX pair computes the parity a xor b xor c onto c, RZ acts on c, then the parity is uncomputed. This uses R_Z(θ)=e^{-iθZ/2}. The overall sign is a convention, and a sign flip equals gamma -> -gamma.
equations.justification: Standard parity-phase gadget; the sign is fixed so that it matches e^{-i gamma C} up to global phase.

equations.label: Objective and satisfied fraction
equations.description: Expected number of satisfied equations. A random string gives m/2. The advantage is the deviation of F/m from 1/2.
equations.abstract_quote: A random string will satisfy 1/2 of the equations.
equations.justification: Follows directly from eq_1 and the abstract's baseline of 1/2.

equations.label: Claimed advantage targets
equations.description: Reference values to compare against the simulated F/m. On tiny instances these asymptotic bounds are only indicative, since D is small.
equations.justification: Both values are stated in the abstract. The typical-case value is quoted from the abstract's second expression.
assumptions: Asymptotic in large D; not expected to be tight for small instances

registers.name: q
registers.role: one qubit per boolean variable, with qubit i = variable i; no ancillas

registers.name: c
registers.role: classical bits for the final readout, with measure(i,i)

specification.initial_state: |0>^n followed by H on every qubit, giving |+>^n

steps.description: Apply H to all n qubits.
For each equation k, apply CX(a,c), CX(b,c), RZ on c with angle ±gamma*s_k, CX(b,c), CX(a,c).
Grid-search (gamma,beta) over the exact statevector expectation F. Initial guesses are gamma ~ 1/sqrt(D) and beta ~ pi/8. Use the maximizing angles.
If counts are required, measure all qubits, sample repeatedly, evaluate the satisfied-equation count of each string classically, and keep the best string.

specification.measurement: Measure all n qubits in the computational basis only if counts are required. Variable i is bits[::-1][i] of the Qiskit counts key. Omit measurements if the statevector is read.
specification.classical_postprocessing: For each sampled z, count the equations with (z_a+z_b+z_c) mod 2 = b_k. Report the mean (an estimate of F) and the best string.
assumptions: Smallest useful instance: a few equations on 4-6 variables, chosen by the later stage
The angle sweep covers both signs, so the RZ sign convention does not matter
No black-box oracle or query; the equations are compiled directly into gates
The qubit count n is under the cap
missing_information: The paper's analytic light-cone formula for <ZZZ> is not given in the abstract. The sketch's form sin(4beta) sin(gamma) cos(gamma)^k is unverified, so I do not state it as an equation.
The exact angles used in the worst-case ln D analysis are not specified.
The explicit rule for choosing gamma and beta in the proofs is not stated in the abstract.
